notes: A whole new look: every window, frame, button and tab now shares one dark, gold-trimmed style, with titles in a carved serif.
Painted icons for every spell and item, on the action bars, in the spellbook, bags, character window, loot, vendors, quest rewards, trades, buffs and talents.
Your frame, your target's and your party's now show portraits: your class's emblem, or the kind of creature you're facing.
Health, mana and experience bars sit in gold-edged troughs, and your target's frame keeps its size whether or not it has mana.
Talents show their icons, glow gold when you can put a point in, and keep their rank in a small badge.
A second zone: Harrowfield, farmland for levels 6 to 12 over the mountain pass south of Ashford Vale, many times the size of the vale.
Harrowfield's village, Wexford, has an inn, a chapel and churchyard, a smithy, trainers for Templars, Clerics and Men-at-Arms, and Hesketh Steele the weaponsmith.

Explore the Coombe farm and its pumpkin patch, the Old Delve and Copperhollow mines, the Mirrow Mere and its mirefin village, Thornwick Tower, the Ashwood lumber camp, the Pellow vineyard, the Reedford landing, the west garrison, a brigand farmstead and the gnoll hills.
Twenty-nine quests in Harrowfield, among them the search for the lost watchmen, the hunt for the Collector, and Grunmaw.
New kinds of quest: explore a place, gather things lying in the world such as Bundles of Wood, and start a quest from an item you find. Some quests begin and end at things rather than people.
New creatures: mirefins, flintback boars, prowlers, young forest bears, Ditchjaw gnolls, brigand cutthroats and hedge-mages, and more. Spiders' bites poison, and gnoll outriders strike twice.
Godric Vane, the Weapon Master by the priory, teaches weapon skills.
A world map: press M to see your zone, your party and where you stand, or pick the whole world.
Menu buttons beside the action bar for Character Info, Spellbook, Talents, Quest Log, Socials, World Map and the Main Menu.
Playerbots travel between zones through the pass and quest in Harrowfield too.
Whisper a playerbot about the item it's selling to get its price. Trades with a playerbot start with the item you talked about already in.
Buffs others cast on you and your party's playerbots are kept when you log out and back in.
The game runs smoothly with many more playerbots, and the Random Bots option now goes up to 400.
Tooltips fit their text, and near the bottom of the screen they appear above the cursor.
Behind-the-scenes testing tools only: nothing changes in play.
Creatures call for help: pull a brigand and its friends close by join in a moment later, and their pulls can bring more.
Some creatures now speak when they attack you. Their words show in the chat under Creature Speech.
Trainers have a Train All button that teaches everything you can afford.
The spellbook is laid out as in the old days: pages of twelve spells, with tabs down its right side for General and each talent tree. It opens under your portrait.
The spellbook has a Hide old ranks box, to show only the highest rank of each spell.
Your target's buffs and debuffs show under its frame. Hover over one to see what it does.
Templars: Boons and Greater Boons buttons in the spellbook open a menu of every boon you know. Put them on your action bar.
Class buffs that lasted 5 minutes or more now last an hour: Boons, Greater Boons, Litany of Fortitude, Uplifted Spirit, Inner Flame, Shadow Warding and more.
Boon icons show the boon's own name, so Boon of Strength and Boon of Shelter look different.
Playerbots treat grey items as junk: they won't try to sell them to you, and they sell them to vendors they pass.
Fixed talent rank numbers drawing over the talent tooltip.
Fixed tooltips getting in the way of the right action bars.
Long patch notes on the login screen now have a scroll bar.
Talents: from level 10 you earn a talent point each level, to spend in your class's three trees. Press N to open the talent window.
Men-at-Arms have Blademastery, Ferocity and Bulwark; Templars Grace, Aegis and Zeal; Clerics Devotion, Mercy and Umbra.
Abilities like Final Stand, Radiant Jolt and Hush now come from talents rather than the trainer. If you bought them before, spend your points to get them back.
Templars have three new talent abilities: Heaven's Favor, Hallowed Presence and Contrition.
Your class trainer can unlearn your talents, for a fee that rises each time.
Playerbots spend their talent points too.
Roots now hold players, playerbots and creatures in place.
Patch note dates are now written month-day-year.
The login screen now shows the notes for the latest patch.
The game now has a version number, shown on the login screen.
Creatures cast spells: Burrowling Firecallers throw Flame Bolts from range, Pickmen pry at your armor, Brigand Footpads stab from behind and Ridgetusk Boars charge.
Interrupt a casting creature with Hilt Strike, Shield Smash, Hush, stuns or fear. The target frame shows what your target is casting.
Stances show in your buffs, the active one is framed in gold, and clicking it again no longer gives an error.
Templars learn Revival's first rank free at level 12, so its higher ranks can be trained.
The Options window is one size, and long pages scroll.
